_comment: Briefs in the shape the tutor hands the explainer (agents/tutor.md, the handoff block; skills/tutor/SKILL.md, 'A missed answer can come back with explain'). pick and right are 0-based option indexes; right is the text itself when no options were offered. identifiers are names from code that a page grounded in the developer's work would use. 'binary': 'runtime' hides eklavya from PATH so only the runtime copy resolves.

cases.stem: A client retries POST /payments after a timeout, sending the same Idempotency-Key. What does the server return the second time?
options: A second charge, because the first request timed out
The stored response from the first request, without charging again
A 409 Conflict, because the key was already used
A 400 Bad Request, because retries must use a fresh key
notes: Treats a timeout as proof nothing happened
Looks the key up and replays what it saved
Rejects any reuse of a key
Puts the burden on the client

cases.stem: The search box calls fetchResults through debounce(fn, 300). The user types five letters 100ms apart. How many requests go out?
options: Five, one per keystroke, each delayed by 300ms
One, 300ms after the last keystroke
Two, one at the first keystroke and one at the last
None, because the user never paused for 300ms
notes: Delays every call instead of collapsing them
Each keystroke restarts the timer
Mixes in leading-edge behaviour
Forgets the timer still fires once typing stops

cases.stem: The orders table has an index on (customer_id, created_at). Which query cannot use that index to find its rows?
options: WHERE customer_id = 7
WHERE customer_id = 7 AND created_at > '2026-01-01'
WHERE created_at > '2026-01-01'
WHERE customer_id = 7 ORDER BY created_at
notes: Uses the first column alone
Uses both columns, left to right
Skips the first column
Filters on the first, sorts on the second

cases.stem: add_tag("a") is called twice on a fresh process, with no tags argument. What does the second call return?
options: ["a"], because each call gets a new empty list
["a", "a"], because the default list is shared between calls
An error, because tags is None the second time
[], because append returns None
notes: Assumes the default is rebuilt per call
The default is built once, when def runs
Confuses this with the None-sentinel fix
Mixes up the return value and the list
cases.code:
# app/tags.py
def add_tag(tag, tags=[]):
    tags.append(tag)
    return tags

cases.stem: useEffect subscribes to a websocket and returns () => socket.close(). When does React call that returned function?
options: Only when the component is removed from the page
Before the effect runs again, and when the component is removed
Right after the effect runs, every render
Never, unless the component calls it
notes: Misses the re-run case
Cleans up the old subscription before each new one
Confuses cleanup with the effect body
Treats it as an ordinary callback

cases.stem: Promise.all([loadUser(), loadOrders(), loadPrefs()]) — loadOrders rejects after 50ms, the others take 200ms. What does the await see, and when?
options: All three results after 200ms, with orders as undefined
The loadOrders rejection after 50ms
The loadOrders rejection after 200ms, once the others finish
An array of three settled results after 200ms
notes: Expects partial results
Rejects as soon as any input rejects
Waits for every input first
Describes Promise.allSettled
cases.typed: it waits for all of them and then throws the orders error

cases.stem: Before Go 1.22, what did this loop print, and why?
cases.right: Usually 3 3 3: every goroutine closes over the same i, and the loop has finished by the time they run

cases.request: Explain how the If-None-Match / 304 thing in our assets handler works. Make me a page on it.

cases.stem: deploy.sh starts with set -e. The line curl -f $URL | tar xz fails because curl gets a 404. What happens next?
options: The script stops, because set -e catches any failing command
The script carries on, because the pipeline's status is tar's
The script stops only if tar also fails, then prints curl's error
Bash retries curl once before giving up
notes: Expects set -e to see inside pipelines
Without pipefail a pipeline reports its last command
Half-right about tar, wrong about the message
Bash has no retry behaviour
cases.code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scripts/deploy.sh
set -e
curl -f "$URL" | tar xz
./install.sh

cases.stem: Why does the compiler reject items.push(4) while first is still in use?
options: Because items is not declared mut
Because first borrows items, and push needs an exclusive borrow while that one is alive
Because push moves items, so first would dangle
Because integers cannot be borrowed
notes: It is declared mut
A shared borrow blocks a mutable one until it ends
push borrows, it does not move
Anything can be borrowed
